from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            'Welcome to the coordinate plane, our mathematical playground.', 
            'Meet Pixel, defined by vectors pointing to his features.', 
            'Transforming means moving every point on Pixel systematically.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: Pixel the Cat and the Grid", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Colors
        GRID_COLOR = "#888888"
        NOSE_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        VECTOR_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        FEATURE_VECTOR_COLOR = "#ADD8E6"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Create coordinate grid
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GRID_COLOR, "stroke_opacity": 0.6},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": GRID_COLOR}
        )
        # Position grid in the right side area
        self.place_in_area(plane, "A1", "F6")
        
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Update lecture highlight
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)

        # Pixel the Cat (Simple shape construction)
        head = Circle(radius=0.4, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.1)
        l_ear = Triangle(color=WHITE).scale(0.12).rotate(30*DEGREES).shift(LEFT*0.25 + UP*0.35)
        r_ear = Triangle(color=WHITE).scale(0.12).rotate(-30*DEGREES).shift(RIGHT*0.25 + UP*0.35)
        nose = Dot(ORIGIN, color=NOSE_COLOR)
        l_eye = Dot(LEFT*0.15 + UP*0.15, color=WHITE, radius=0.03)
        r_eye = Dot(RIGHT*0.15 + UP*0.15, color=WHITE, radius=0.03)
        
        pixel_group = VGroup(head, l_ear, r_ear, nose, l_eye, r_eye)
        
        # Position Pixel such that his nose is at vector [1, 1] relative to the grid
        pixel_group.shift(plane.c2p(1,1) - nose.get_center())
        
        self.play(FadeIn(pixel_group))
        self.play(Indicate(nose, color=NOSE_COLOR, scale_factor=1.5))
        
        # Vector arrow from origin to nose
        vec_to_nose = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), nose.get_center(), color=VECTOR_COLOR, buff=0)
        self.play(GrowArrow(vec_to_nose))
        
        # Several vectors pointing to other features (ears and eyes)
        feat_vectors = VGroup()
        feature_points = [l_ear.get_top(), r_ear.get_top(), l_eye.get_center(), r_eye.get_center()]
        for pt in feature_points:
            feat_vectors.add(Arrow(
                plane.c2p(0,0), pt, 
                color=FEATURE_VECTOR_COLOR, 
                buff=0, 
                stroke_width=2, 
                max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.15
            ))
            
        self.play(Create(feat_vectors))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Update lecture highlight
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)

        # Define a linear transformation matrix (Shear + Scale)
        # Systematic movement of every point
        matrix = [[1.2, 0.4], [0.2, 0.9]]
        
        # Group everything to transform together
        all_graphics = VGroup(plane, pixel_group, vec_to_nose, feat_vectors)
        
        # Perform the transformation
        self.play(
            all_graphics.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            run_time=3
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title_text = "Prerequisite: The Power of Basis Vectors"
        lecture_lines = [
            'Every point lives as a combination of basis vectors.',
            'Meet i-hat, the unit vector along the x-axis.',
            'Meet j-hat, the unit vector along the y-axis.',
            'Any coordinate (x, y) scales these two basis arrows.',
            'To track movement, we only watch these two vectors.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Configuration
        I_HAT_COLOR = "#FF0000"
        J_HAT_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        LABEL_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        
        # Background Grid (Right Side)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 5, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=4.5,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.25}
        ).set_z_index(-1)
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6')
        origin = plane.c2p(0, 0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Every point lives as a combination of basis vectors.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Meet i-hat, the unit vector along the x-axis.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        i_hat = Arrow(origin, plane.c2p(1, 0), buff=0, color=I_HAT_COLOR, stroke_width=6)
        i_label = Text("i-hat", font_size=18, color=LABEL_COLOR).next_to(i_hat, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_hat), Write(i_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Meet j-hat, the unit vector along the y-axis.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        j_hat = Arrow(origin, plane.c2p(0, 1), buff=0, color=J_HAT_COLOR, stroke_width=6)
        j_label = Text("j-hat", font_size=18, color=LABEL_COLOR).next_to(j_hat, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(j_hat), Write(j_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Any coordinate (x, y) scales these two basis arrows.
        # Action: Show point (3,2). Animate red and green components.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        target_pt = [3, 2]
        dot = Dot(plane.c2p(*target_pt), color=WHITE, radius=0.08)
        coord_label = Text("(3, 2)", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(dot, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        # Scaling paths
        red_arrows = VGroup(*[
            Arrow(plane.c2p(k, 0), plane.c2p(k+1, 0), buff=0, color=I_HAT_COLOR, stroke_width=3)
            for k in range(3)
        ])
        green_arrows = VGroup(*[
            Arrow(plane.c2p(3, k), plane.c2p(3, k+1), buff=0, color=J_HAT_COLOR, stroke_width=3)
            for k in range(2)
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(dot), Write(coord_label))
        self.play(Succession(*[GrowArrow(arr) for arr in red_arrows], run_time=1.2))
        self.play(Succession(*[GrowArrow(arr) for arr in green_arrows], run_time=0.8))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # To track movement, we only watch these two vectors.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Pulse the basis vectors
        self.play(
            Indicate(i_hat, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, scale_factor=1.2),
            Indicate(j_hat, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, scale_factor=1.2),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with provided lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Rules of Linear Transformation", 
            [
                "A transformation is linear if the origin stays fixed.", 
                "Grid lines must remain straight, parallel, and evenly spaced.", 
                "This ensures space stretches without warping into curves."
            ]
        )
        
        # Visual color palette
        COLOR_1 = YELLOW
        COLOR_2 = TEAL
        COLOR_3 = "#FF69B4" 
        FLASH_COLOR = "#90EE90"
        
        # Initialize the coordinate grid mobject
        # We use a NumberPlane as the visual "grid"
        grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": BLUE_C,
                "stroke_width": 2,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.5
            },
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "stroke_opacity": 0.7}
        )
        # Position grid in the right side area (A1 to F6)
        self.place_in_area(grid, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        grid_center = grid.get_center()

        # Origin marker dot
        origin_dot = Dot(grid_center, radius=0.12, color=WHITE).set_z_index(10)
        origin_label = Text("Origin (0,0)", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        origin_label.next_to(origin_dot, DOWN, buff=0.15)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "A transformation is linear if the origin stays fixed."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_1),
            Create(grid),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            FadeIn(origin_dot),
            Write(origin_label),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        
        # Demonstrating fixed origin via rotation
        self.play(
            Rotate(grid, angle=30*DEGREES, about_point=grid_center),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Grid lines must remain straight, parallel, and evenly spaced."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_2),
            FadeOut(origin_label),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        
        # Apply a shear matrix to simulate tilting while preserving parallelism
        shear_matrix = np.array([[1, 0.6, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]])
        
        def linear_tilt(p):
            # Transform relative to the grid center (which is the origin)
            relative_p = p - grid_center
            new_p = np.dot(shear_matrix, relative_p)
            return new_p + grid_center

        self.play(
            grid.animate.apply_function(linear_tilt),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "This ensures space stretches without warping into curves."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_3),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        
        # Show non-linear warping (violation of linearity)
        def warp_logic(p):
            relative_p = p - grid_center
            x, y, z = relative_p
            # Add sinusoidal distortion to curve the lines
            new_x = x + 0.4 * np.sin(y * 2.0)
            new_y = y + 0.4 * np.cos(x * 2.0)
            return np.array([new_x, new_y, z]) + grid_center

        self.play(
            grid.animate.apply_function(warp_logic),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=wiggle
        )
        
        # Create a fresh linear grid for the snap back
        clean_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": BLUE_C,
                "stroke_width": 2,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.5
            },
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "stroke_opacity": 0.7}
        )
        self.place_in_area(clean_grid, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Visual flash effect for the "snap"
        flash_effect = Rectangle(
            width=5.2, height=5.2, 
            stroke_width=0, 
            fill_color=FLASH_COLOR, 
            fill_opacity=0.4
        ).move_to(grid_center)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(flash_effect),
            ReplacementTransform(grid, clean_grid),
            run_time=0.25
        )
        self.play(FadeOut(flash_effect), run_time=0.4)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title = "Encoding Motion into a Matrix"
        lines = [
            'A 2x2 matrix encodes where basis vectors land.',
            'The first column tracks the new position of i-hat.',
            'The second column tracks the new position of j-hat.',
            'This bracketed grid serves as a transformation instruction manual.',
            'Together, they define how the entire plane shifts.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        I_HAT_COLOR = "#FF0000"
        J_HAT_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight lecture
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Grid area for the plane: A1 to D4
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        ).scale(0.5)
        
        self.place_in_area(plane, "A1", "D4")
        
        # Basis vectors
        i_hat = Vector([1, 0], color=I_HAT_COLOR)
        j_hat = Vector([0, 1], color=J_HAT_COLOR)
        
        # Shift vectors to plane position
        plane_center = plane.get_center()
        i_hat.shift(plane_center)
        j_hat.shift(plane_center)
        
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1)
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_hat), GrowArrow(j_hat))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Matrix setup in area E2 to F5
        # Replacing MathTex with Text to bypass missing LaTeX installation
        bracket_l = Text("[", font_size=80)
        bracket_r = Text("]", font_size=80)
        self.place_at_grid(bracket_l, "C5", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(bracket_r, "C6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Move i_hat to (2, 1) relative to plane
        new_i_pos = plane.coords_to_point(2, 1)
        
        self.play(i_hat.animate.put_start_and_end_on(plane_center, new_i_pos))
        
        # Show coordinates (2, 1) next to tip using Text
        coord_i = Text("(2, 1)", color=I_HAT_COLOR, font_size=24).next_to(new_i_pos, UR, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Write(coord_i))
        
        # Numbers to move into matrix using Text
        val_i1 = Text("2", color=I_HAT_COLOR, font_size=36)
        val_i2 = Text("1", color=I_HAT_COLOR, font_size=36)
        
        # Target positions in matrix
        pos_i1 = self.grid["B5"] + RIGHT*0.5
        pos_i2 = self.grid["D5"] + RIGHT*0.5
        
        self.play(Write(bracket_l), Write(bracket_r))
        self.play(
            val_i1.animate.move_to(pos_i1),
            val_i2.animate.move_to(pos_i2),
            FadeOut(coord_i)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Move j_hat to (-1, 1)
        new_j_pos = plane.coords_to_point(-1, 1)
        
        self.play(j_hat.animate.put_start_and_end_on(plane_center, new_j_pos))
        
        # Show coordinates (-1, 1) using Text
        coord_j = Text("(-1, 1)", color=J_HAT_COLOR, font_size=24).next_to(new_j_pos, UL, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Write(coord_j))
        
        # Numbers for matrix using Text
        val_j1 = Text("-1", color=J_HAT_COLOR, font_size=36)
        val_j2 = Text("1", color=J_HAT_COLOR, font_size=36)
        
        # Target positions Column 2
        pos_j1 = self.grid["B6"] - RIGHT*0.5
        pos_j2 = self.grid["D6"] - RIGHT*0.5
        
        self.play(
            val_j1.animate.move_to(pos_j1),
            val_j2.animate.move_to(pos_j2),
            FadeOut(coord_j)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Pulse the matrix
        matrix_all = VGroup(bracket_l, bracket_r, val_i1, val_i2, val_j1, val_j2)
        self.play(matrix_all.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(matrix_all.animate.scale(1/1.1), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Define the matrix for the transformation
        matrix = [[2, -1], [1, 1]]

class CustomMathText(Text):
    def __init__(self, tex_string, **kwargs):
        # Basic cleanup of LaTeX commands for Text compatibility
        clean_string = (
            tex_string.replace(r"\cdot", "·")
            .replace(r"\hat{i}", "i-hat")
            .replace(r"\hat{j}", "j-hat")
            .replace(r"_{new}", " new")
            .replace(r"\\", "\n")
            .replace(r"\vec{v}", "v")
        )
        super().__init__(clean_string, **kwargs)

class CustomMatrix(VGroup):
    def __init__(self, matrix_data, **kwargs):
        super().__init__()
        element_to_mobject = kwargs.pop("element_to_mobject", Text)
        left_bracket_str = kwargs.pop("left_bracket", "[")
        right_bracket_str = kwargs.pop("right_bracket", "]")
        
        # Build the elements
        rows = []
        for r in matrix_data:
            row_mobs = VGroup(*[element_to_mobject(str(item), font_size=24) for item in r]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.6)
            rows.append(row_mobs)
        
        self.elements_group = VGroup(*rows).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
        
        # Create brackets using Text mobjects
        l_bracket = Text(left_bracket_str, font_size=40)
        l_bracket.stretch_to_fit_height(self.elements_group.height + 0.3)
        l_bracket.next_to(self.elements_group, LEFT, buff=0.15)
        
        r_bracket = Text(right_bracket_str, font_size=40)
        r_bracket.stretch_to_fit_height(self.elements_group.height + 0.3)
        r_bracket.next_to(self.elements_group, RIGHT, buff=0.15)
        
        self.add(l_bracket, r_bracket, self.elements_group)

class Section5Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title
        title = CustomMathText("Linear Transformations and Matrices", font_size=36)
        title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        # 2. Setup Coordinate System
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-7, 7, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": BLUE_D,
                "stroke_width": 1,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.5
            }
        )
        
        # 3. Initial Basis Vectors
        i_hat = Vector([1, 0], color=GREEN)
        j_hat = Vector([0, 1], color=RED)
        i_label = CustomMathText(r"\hat{i}", color=GREEN, font_size=22).next_to(i_hat, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        j_label = CustomMathText(r"\hat{j}", color=RED, font_size=22).next_to(j_hat, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # 4. Matrix Display (2x2 Transformation Matrix)
        # Transformation: i_hat -> [2, -1], j_hat -> [1, 1]
        matrix_data = [[2, 1], [-1, 1]]
        matrix_mob = CustomMatrix(matrix_data)
        matrix_mob.to_corner(UL, buff=0.7).shift(DOWN * 0.8)
        matrix_header = Text("Matrix A:", font_size=22).next_to(matrix_mob, UP, aligned_edge=LEFT)

        # Animations
        self.add(plane)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(i_hat), 
            GrowArrow(j_hat), 
            FadeIn(i_label), 
            FadeIn(j_label)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(matrix_header),
            FadeIn(matrix_mob)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # 5. Perform the Transformation
        target_i = np.array([2, -1, 0])
        target_j = np.array([1, 1, 0])

        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_data),
            i_hat.animate.put_start_and_end_on(ORIGIN, target_i),
            j_hat.animate.put_start_and_end_on(ORIGIN, target_j),
            i_label.animate.move_to(target_i + DOWN * 0.4),
            j_label.animate.move_to(target_j + UP * 0.4),
            run_time=3
        )
        
        # Conclusion labels
        transformed_text = Text("The matrix determines where basis vectors land.", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        transformed_text.to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(transformed_text))
        self.wait(3)

class Section6Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and bullet points
        self.setup_layout(
            "Linear Transformations & Matrices", 
            [
                "- Matrices as functions",
                "- Mapping basis vectors",
                "- Transforming space"
            ]
        )
        
        # 1. Visualization of a Linear Transformation
        grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": BLUE_D,
                "stroke_width": 2,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.5
            }
        )
        
        # Place the grid on the right side using the custom layout logic
        self.place_at_grid(grid, "C4", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Basis vectors
        i_hat = Vector([1, 0], color=GREEN)
        j_hat = Vector([0, 1], color=RED)
        
        # Transformation matrix [[1, 1], [0, 1]] (Shear)
        matrix = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        
        self.play(Create(grid))
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_hat.move_to(grid.c2p(0,0), aligned_edge=DOWN+LEFT)), 
                  GrowArrow(j_hat.move_to(grid.c2p(0,0), aligned_edge=DOWN+LEFT)))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Apply shear transformation to the grid and vectors
        self.play(
            grid.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            i_hat.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            j_hat.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Background and Title
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=24, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define animation grid (6x6) on the right side of the screen
        # X: 1 to 5, Y: 2 to -2
        self.grid_map = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Offset x to the right half of the screen
                x_pos = 1.5 + (j * 0.8)
                y_pos = 2.0 - (i * 0.8)
                self.grid_map[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x_pos, y_pos, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        if grid_pos in self.grid_map:
            mobject.move_to(self.grid_map[grid_pos])
        else:
            mobject.move_to(RIGHT * 3)

outline.topic: Linear Transformations and Matrices: The Visual Language of Motion
outline.target_audience: First-year university students or advanced high school students

sections.title: Introduction: Pixel the Cat and the Grid
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a coordinate plane as a playground. We represent a character (Pixel the Cat) using vectors that point to specific coordinates (e.g., the tip of the ear, the nose). Establish that 'transforming' means moving every point on Pixel to a new location systematically.
sections.example: Visualize Pixel the Cat standing on a standard grid. His nose is at the vector [1, 1]. To make him 'jump' or 'stretch', we need a mathematical function that takes his current position and outputs a new one.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Power of Basis Vectors
sections.content: Explain that every point in 2D space is just a combination of two standard basis vectors: i-hat (1, 0) and j-hat (0, 1). To understand any complex movement, we only need to see what happens to these two tiny arrows.
sections.example: Show i-hat as a red arrow on the x-axis and j-hat as a green arrow on the y-axis. Any point (x, y) is visually shown as walking 'x' steps along the red arrow and 'y' steps along the green arrow.

sections.title: The Rules of Linear Transformation
sections.content: Define 'Linearity' visually. A transformation is linear if: 1. The origin (0,0) remains fixed. 2. All grid lines remain straight, parallel, and evenly spaced. This ensures the 'grid' doesn't warp into curves.
sections.example: An animation showing the grid tilting or stretching. If the grid lines were to curve like a funhouse mirror, it would no longer be a 'linear' transformation.

sections.title: Encoding Motion into a Matrix
sections.content: Introduce the 2x2 Matrix as a 'data container' for where i-hat and j-hat land after the transformation. The first column is the new coordinates of i-hat; the second column is the new coordinates of j-hat.
sections.example: If i-hat lands at (2, 1) and j-hat lands at (-1, 1), we write them side-by-side in a bracket. This 2x2 grid of numbers is the 'Matrix'—a compact instruction manual for the transformation.

sections.title: The Calculation: Transforming Pixel
sections.content: Demonstrate matrix-vector multiplication as a 'recipe'. To find Pixel’s new nose position, we take his original coordinates and mix the new basis vectors accordingly.
sections.example: Pixel’s nose was at (1, 1). Using our matrix, the new nose position is 1* (new i-hat) + 1* (new j-hat). Calculation: [2, 1] + [-1, 1] = [1, 2]. Visually show the nose moving to the new spot on the tilted grid.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
sections.content: Recap that matrices aren't just boxes of numbers; they are descriptions of how space is manipulated. Mention that this is exactly how video games rotate characters or how filters warp photos.
sections.example: A montage of Pixel the Cat rotating, shearing, and scaling rapidly, with the corresponding 2x2 matrices flashing on screen to show the 'code' behind the movement.

storyboard.title: Introduction: Pixel the Cat and the Grid
lecture_lines: Welcome to the coordinate plane, our mathematical playground.
Meet Pixel, our character positioned at the grid center.
A vector arrow locates his nose precisely in space.
Multiple vectors together define his entire visual shape.
Transforming means moving every point in a systematic way.
animations: Fade in a coordinate grid (#888888) with Pixel the Cat (a simple shape) at the center.
Draw a white vector (#FFFFFF) to Pixel's nose and several light blue vectors (#ADD8E6) to his features.
Animate the entire grid and Pixel shifting together to a new position.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Power of Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: Meet the basis vectors, i-hat and j-hat, our building blocks.
Scale these arrows to reach any point in space.
We label these unit vectors i-hat and j-hat.
animations: Show a coordinate grid (#444444) and a white dot (#FFFFFF) at (3, 2) to represent a generic point.
Animate a red arrow (#FF0000) from (0,0) to (1,0) labeled 'i-hat' in white (#FFFFFF).
Animate a green arrow (#00FF00) from (0,0) to (0,1) labeled 'j-hat' in white (#FFFFFF).
Show the red arrow scaling to length 3 and green arrow scaling to length 2, summing to reach the point (3, 2).
Highlight the original i-hat (#FF0000) and j-hat (#00FF00) vectors with a yellow flash (#FFFF00).

storyboard.title: The Rules of Linear Transformation
lecture_lines: A transformation is linear if the origin stays fixed.
Grid lines must remain straight, parallel, and evenly spaced.
This ensures space stretches without warping into curves.
animations: Show a grid. Keep the origin point (0,0) as a large white dot (#FFFFFF).
Animate the grid lines tilting while remaining straight, parallel, and evenly spaced.
Briefly show the grid lines curving wildly, then snap them back to being straight with a green flash (#90EE90).

storyboard.title: Encoding Motion into a Matrix
lecture_lines: We start with the standard basis vectors on the grid.
Watch as i-hat and j-hat move to new locations.
A 2x2 matrix records these final basis positions.
The first column captures the coordinates of transformed i-hat.
The second column captures the coordinates of transformed j-hat.
animations: Display the standard i-hat (#FF0000) and j-hat (#00FF00) unit vectors on a static grid.
Animate i-hat moving to (2, 1) and j-hat moving to (-1, 1) as the grid transforms.
Show a pair of empty matrix brackets [ ] appearing on the right side of the screen.
Animate the coordinates of the new i-hat (2, 1) moving into the first column of the matrix (#FF0000).
Animate the coordinates of the new j-hat (-1, 1) moving into the second column of the matrix (#00FF00).

storyboard.title: The Calculation: Transforming Pixel
lecture_lines: Matrix multiplication is a recipe for transforming any point.
Highlight the first column and the original x-coordinate.
Scale the new i-hat by his original x-coordinate.
Add the new j-hat scaled by his original y-coordinate.
His nose lands precisely at its new calculated location.
animations: Display the 2x2 matrix and Pixel's nose vector [1, 1] side-by-side as a calculation.
Highlight the first column of the matrix and the nose's original x-coordinate (1).
Show the transformed i-hat vector [2, 1] being scaled by the nose's x-coordinate.
Scale the transformed j-hat [-1, 1] by the nose's y-coordinate (1) and visually sum the vectors.
Move the blue nose dot (#0000FF) to the resulting position [1, 2] on the transformed grid.

storyboard.title: Summary and Real-World Application
lecture_lines: Matrices describe how we manipulate space and shapes.
This math powers video game graphics and photo filters.
Linear transformations bring the digital world to life.
animations: Show Pixel the Cat rotating 45 degrees. Display a rotation matrix in yellow (#FFFF00).
Show Pixel stretching horizontally. Display a scaling matrix in yellow (#FFFF00).
Fade out everything and display 'Linear Transformations' in center with gold color (#FFD700).
